//: ECS Fargate task definition for the API. Placeholders of the form ${NAME} are substituted by deploy.sh from deploy/aws/env.sh. Registered with: aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://rendered.json
//cpu: 1 vCPU / 2 GB is the smallest size that comfortably runs the export writer, which holds one batch plus a workbook in memory.
//runtimePlatform: ARM64 targets Graviton, which is about 20% cheaper than X86_64 for the same work. The Dockerfile cross-compiles for it. Change both this and the --platform in deploy.sh together, or the task will fail to start with an exec format error.
//executionRoleArn: Pulls the image and reads the secrets below. Needs AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy plus secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secrets.
//taskRoleArn: What the application itself is allowed to do: s3:GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject on the bucket prefix, and nothing else. This is why no AWS key appears anywhere in this file.

volumes.//: An empty ephemeral volume, not a tmpfs - Fargate does not support tmpfs. It exists so /tmp stays writable under readonlyRootFilesystem, which the export writer needs: it streams each file to disk before uploading rather than holding a few hundred megabytes in memory.
volumes.name: tmp

containerDefinitions.name: api
containerDefinitions.//readonlyRootFilesystem: Safe only because Storage:Provider is S3. With the local provider the application creates and writes its storage directory and would fail at start-up.
containerDefinitions.//stopTimeout: ECS sends SIGTERM, waits, then SIGKILL. The default 30s can cut off an in-flight export; 120 gives it room. An export killed anyway is recovered by the stalled-job sweep, so this is politeness rather than correctness.

environment.//: The API serves requests; the worker service runs the schedule. Two API tasks with the scheduler on would dispatch every campaign twice.
environment.name: Scheduler__Enabled

environment.//: Never true with more than one task: several instances race to migrate the same database while the previous version is still serving. deploy.sh runs the migration as its own task first.
environment.name: Database__ApplyMigrationsOnStartup

environment.//: SignalR across more than one task requires the backplane. Without it a client connected to task A never receives an export-finished event raised on task B, and the toast simply never arrives.
environment.name: Redis__Enabled

containerDefinitions.//secrets: Injected as environment variables by the execution role at start-up. The values never appear in the task definition, in CloudFormation, or in `aws ecs describe-task-definition` output.
containerDefinitions.//healthCheck: The container-level check. The load balancer runs its own against /health/ready; this one is liveness, so a slow database does not make ECS kill a healthy task.
